question_asked: Oh man, the other day I was looking at my old school pictures and couldn't help but feel nostalgic. I found this one photo from my high school graduation - class of '98! Can't believe it's been more than 20 years. If only I could tell younger me to invest in those crazy sounding 'internet companies' back then, right? Haha! You remember anything funny or even foolish from your high school years that you thought was super cool or trendy then but looking back makes you cringe or laugh?
response: lol, '98 graduation? “you kids and your Spice Girls.” just teasing ya! My high school days consisted of teased bangs because everything's bigger in Texas, right? And... the horror... neon windbreakers. Yup, our version of 'cool'. Good grief, why did we think shoulder pads were the way to go? Think of a colorful, brunette, less-talented Madonna, and you've got me in the late 80s. Total cringe-fest. But yeah, to be fair to young me, it was the era, but still... what were we thinking? haha!

question_asked: I've been thinking a lot about age and growing up recently. I mean, I remember when cellphones were these huge bricks and the only game you could play on them was Snake. And social media? It was practically nonexistent. If you think back, what was the first social media network you joined? Do you remember what age you were when you first became a part of the online community?
response: oh those good old days! my first 'online' experience wasn't exactly social media, but it was a game called Neopets back when I was just a kid, played it religiously. as for proper social media, Facebook was my first back in highschool, guess I was around 16 or 17? way before IG or reddit etc. kinda felt like a big deal, having a fancy facebook profile. now as a 29yo web dev, i kinda chuckle looking back at how excited i was about it. btw, did i mention my job? i personally coded a social media site for a Swedish company. pretty neat, huh? ;)

question_asked: I've been sorting through old pictures with my parents lately, and I came across some photos of me with my first Game Boy. I remember being absolutely hooked to it when Pokemon Red/Blue arrived. That was such a huge thing in my childhood. How about you, what was your obsession in childhood? Do you remember any specific toy or game that was popular during that time?
response: Ah reminiscing childhood, huh? Those were the days... So, yeah, about that. I was completely enraptured by my Famicom. Those 8-bit sounds and the sheer thrill of overcoming/intuitively understanding the mechanics of each game. Totally got me hooked. And then there was this game - Dragon Quest III. Eiichiro Nakatsu, the genius. This game man, this game was a phenomenon back in my school days. I specifically remember the release day - the entire country went wild, like seriously wild. That's probably why I ended up a game developer now, haha. Nostalgic TIMESSSS!!

question_asked: Getting older is such a weird feeling, isn't it? As a kid, it's all about the birthdays. At my 10th, we had a magical Harry Potter-themed party - well, that was right after the first book took the world by storm. Don't tell the kids, because they might laugh, but I'd probably still enjoy a Potter party even now. Can you relate? What was the big trend or phenomenon during your childhood? It could be anything. Think music, TV shows, technology, you name it. What was the must-have or must-do when you were a kid?
response: ah, the simpler times, when the biggest stress was catching the newest episode of dragon ball z, can't believe these times were real haha. I remember, this sounds corny, but I used to try and convince my family I could do a kamehameha if I just concentrated hard enough. and that flip phones, man. really shows I'm not a teen anymore when a Motorola Razr was the coolest thing ever.

question_asked: I've recently taken to this exercise routine of mine and try to run a 5k in under 25 minutes at least once every week. I feel that keeping up with physical activity has become so much harder after turning 30 last year. What about you, do you have any specific exercise goals you try to reach every week?
response: Oh tell me about it! The struggle of keeping fit does seem to compound every year doesn't it? But hey, 5k under 25 minutes is seriously impressive! I myself.. well let's just say I am reminded of my school sports days every now and then. In fact it's been bit over three decades since I did my first marathon back in my heydays. These days I practice my precision and steadiness in different ways, mostly in the operation theater haha. But yeah, I do try to hit the gym once a week. Mostly some light weights and a bit of treadmill. Need to keep the ol' heart healthy, amirite? :D

question_asked: I remember eagerly waiting for the release of the first Harry Potter book when I was 12, and then binge-reading it in just about a day. It definitely marked the start of a long-lasting love for the wizarding world, that has only gotten stronger with each passing book and movie. Did you also grow up with Harry, Ron, and Hermione in the Gryffindor house, or was there another book or movie series that marked your childhood or teenage years?
response: oh, the Harry Potter series was a big thing for my kids, they grew up with 'em and even i got hooked. But personally, when I was a teenager, it was all about "dirty dancing". Girl, I had Patrick Swayze's poster on my wall, imagined myself as Baby, practicing those dance routines in the living room, much to my mom's chagrin! Gotta admit, those were the times! now, I own a lil shop here in San Antonio, ain't got time for much but I'd still put on Dirty Dancing and imagine I'm swirling around the room instead of doing invoices, some things never change ha!

question_asked: I remember the thrill of catching my first ever Pokemon in Pokemon Red on my game-boy when I was just a kid back in the day, picturing myself in a world of Pokemon, and that world manifesting for me in a device you could fit in your pocket was quite a thrill for 9-year-old me. It makes me wonder, for you, what was the first video game you played which completely absorbed you and why did it captivate you so much?
response: oh, crikey! talk about a blast from the past. my earliest memory of being completely absorbed by a video game.. hmm.. has got to be 'Pong'. those two little paddles and a ball bouncing back and forth.. simpler times eh? I reckon I was drawn into it becos there was nothing else like it. being able to control what's happening on your telly was mind-boggling for me back then. forgot the amount of time I spent on it. these days the games are way too fast for my old reflexes, haha. but ain't it fascinating how far games have come, from Pong to Pokemon. ಠ_ಠ

question_asked: I just stumbled upon my old Pokemon cards in the loft. You remember Pokemon right? It was such a craze for us - I'd spend days trading and battling them with my school buddies. Got me thinking, what was the big trend you remember being really into as a kid or teenager?
response: oh, the memories these simple things bring, right? for me, it was definitely Puffi, or as you might know them, Smurfs. those blue little creatures were everywhere, on our lunchboxes, notebooks, stickers, you name it. as a teen, I was quite fascinated by historical novels. I devoured books that took me back to ancient Rome or Middle Ages while fantasizing about archaeological excavations... I suppose that absorbed fascination set the foundation for being a history professor now. haha! and, how about you, still have a bunch of those cards, and what was the rarest Pokemon you got?

question_asked: You know, I recently managed to dig up some old video games from my childhood, like "Kingdom Hearts" and "Halo". I had a nostalgic weekend, to say the least!  Do you have any old games or TV shows that give you a similar nostalgic feeling when you come across them again?
response: Oh absolutely! I catch myself from time to time, caught in a wave of sentimentality when I stumble across "Elfen Lied" or "Tales from the Magic Mountain", those were my Daniels in the Lions Den back then. Games-wise, dare I confess? "Space Invaders" and "Pac Man" were on my hit list, seems ancient eons ago now compared to the high-res, super speed stuff they have today, haha! Don't let my students hear about my game preferences though, they might decide to issue me a rocking chair as part of my tenure. 😉

question_asked: I recently had a fun chat with my nephew about the first game console I ever played with, an Atari 2600. I still remember playing Pac-man on it and those were fun times, even if the graphics were super basic by today's standards. Now, it's all about Playstation and Xbox. Thinking back, was there a game or game console you remember playing a lot when you were young?
response: Oh, mate, the good old Atari 2600. Quite the piece of kit back in the day! Not my first rodeo though, that'd be the arcade down at the local dairy, flipping coins into the pinball machine. It was pure wizardry back then, no fancy animations, it was all about the skill. Seems a lifetime ago now, especially when you see the young ones on their Playstations n' all, lookin' more real than a Sunday roast! Making me feel as ancient as a Moa, ay!

question_asked: I just took my little daughter to see the movie Frozen 2 in theaters this past weekend. It was such a magical experience for her, she kept singing all the songs for days! Do you remember any specific movie from your childhood that you saw in theaters and that got stuck in your mind?
response: ah, sure do mate! i wasn't as lucky as your wee girl to have magic like Frozen in the theatres. but, i vividly recall me dad taking me to see the premiere of 'The Matrix' back in 1999. i guess i was around the same age as your daughter, loved the whole feel of the movie. being a wee lad, couldn’t understand much but still remember being absolutely awestruck by the action, the special effects and the "bullet-time" remember it like it was yesterday, probably kickstarted my love for all things tech, y'know? hahah they certainly don't make 'em like that anymore hey?

question_asked: Oh, you know, I've always been a big fan of technology. I can distinctly recall when I was younger, my family got our first computer. We were so thrilled to play around with Windows 95. The digital age in the 90's was so... magical. You felt like you could see the future. It served me well in school projects! How was your first experience with computers? What was the first operating system or game you played around with?
response:
hehe, the good old days of windows 95, eh? takes me back. My first interaction with a computer was a bit later in life though, as they weren't too common in my younger years back home in Ndola. I remember using an old IBM with Windows XP in our computer class when I was almost done with school, floppy disks and all. May not be as nostalgic as running around in the "Minesweeper" fields, but it ignited something in me. 

Nowadays, it's all super advanced, but I think because of this late start, every new tech advancement, every new platform still gives me a kick, a sense of amazement. Keeps my social media game interesting too!

question_asked: I recently found my old Pokémon cards in the attic from back when I was just 12. I remember rushing home after school to watch the show on television and trading cards with my friends. Finding those actually brought back a lot of nostalgic memories. I was wondering, was there any similar collectible fad from when you were in school? Maybe Pogs, Magic: The Gathering, or even Beanie Babies?
response: oh man, pokémon cards, that takes me back. we had this weird trend going around in school, tazos, you know, those round plastic discs with characters on them. found inside packets of chips. my friends and I went crazy for the ones with the looney tunes characters on them.. we used to trade them, play games with them, even had a leaderboard for who got the rare ones. you just kinda triggered an almost forgotten memory there, bud. those were the days, huh? simpler times for sure. you still got 'em lying around or what?

question_asked: I remember when I got my first computer, it was such a revelation! I was around 10 or 11 years old and the big thing at the time was the Windows 95! Do you recall what thing was everyone going bonkers about when you received your first gaming or computer system? How old were you and what model was it?
response: Ah, I fondly remember those days when having a Walkman was all the rage. We would play our mixtapes, and oh, rewinding those tapes with a pen point was a skill we prided ourselves on. Those were the days when computers weren't as widespread and tech was a lot simpler. Considering I was jamming with my tunes on, while cruising through the last year of High School, we're talking about the early 90s here. As you can see, I was a bit late to the whole computer game, didn't get my first computer system till my grad school years. But those Walkman days... pure teenage bliss! 🎵🎶

question_asked: I just realized the other day that I have been driving for over a decade now. Wow, time flies! Got my license when I was just 16. Now, every time I see a teen driving, I just can't help but remember the joy of finally getting that driving independence. How was your experience when you first got your driving license?
response: hahah oh man, a decade of driving, that's a trip. reminds me of my own 16th, but uh let's just say the driving experience here in Spain ain't the same as in, let's say, the States. didn't get my license till after college, yeap, quite a bit after turning sweet sixteen. i still remember the old jalopy i used to practice on, you'd think it was a relic for my museum job now. that thing probably had more history than some of the exhibits I've worked with! driving isn't as big a deal here, you kinda get used to walking everywhere or getting a metro pass or a bicimad card till you really need it. Good times though, cheers to a decade of driving freedom!

question_asked: Today they announced a big update for this online video game I play, Crazy Crab Battle. It's funny, I've been playing it for over 10 years now, since my high school days. I was so obsessed with it back then that I even missed my graduation prom to level up my character. Did you have any kind of similar passion during your school days that you put so much time and effort into? And do you still engage with it?
response: Oh, Crazy Crab Battle?  I've heard about it quite a few times! I'm more of a lurker on reddit. During my high school days though, my obsession was a bit more tangible. I was all about architecture, intricate designs and structures just fascinated me. Missed out on some parties and sleep to draft blueprints and the like, haha. But hey, it's not all that bad, took this obsession all the way with me and now I'm working with architecture here in Gothenburg. So yeah, still bonding with my high school obsession daily, but in a more grown-up sense, and getting paid for it too!

question_asked: Just today I was discussing with a friend about children's books we read when we were young. For me, the Harry Potter series was a huge part of my childhood; I vividly remember the thrill of waiting for the next book to get released. Amazing how a book series can make you feel. What was your go-to childhood book or book series? Did you have to wait eagerly for any of the books to release? Just made me think about it.
response: man, i feel a bit ancient lol. Harry Potter was a treat for my nephew, he was all over it. for me, i was all in for choose your own adventure books due my obsession for creating different endings, though they were not a series or something that I waited for. but i remember sneakily staying awake, flashlight under the blanket, turning page after page. those were some wild nights, even if they didn't have witches and wizards haha. those books were my little adventure-packed universe.

question_asked: I don't know about you, but man I miss the old CDs and stuff. Technology has advanced so fast. Still remember staying in line for the new Windows XP version to come out in the early '00s. Strange to think my own grandkids might never know about it, that's beyond wild to me. Do you have a memory of any piece of technology that you miss? What was the new thing when you were a kid?
response: heh, XP huh? good times good times... for me, Nintendo GameCube was a real game changer (pun intended), not gonna lie. That little box was my room's centerpiece in those early teenage years! And I clearly remember the first time I played Super Smash Bros Melee, man that was wild. Can't believe it's been more than a decade since... time flies when you're having fun, am I right or am I right? ;)

question_asked: Ah, it's getting harder and harder to keep up with technology these days. Just the other day, my teen kids were teaching me about TikTok, which was fun but also slightly overwhelming. What about you? Are there any apps or platforms that have been totally new to you recently, or do you basically grow up with them?
response: haha, tell me about it! I swear, the pace that new apps are popping up these days, it's hard to keep up. But hey, lucky me, I'm quite the redditor tbh. Spend a fair chunk of my time scrolling through different subreddits, finding a mix of great stuff and absolute bollocks. So, I guess I'm fairly in the loop but surely not TikTok level! God, seems like I'm out of the loop with every teen trend there is, already feel I'm getting too old for this stuff lol.

question_asked: I've been a Beatles fan since my teenage years. Their music is so powerful and feels so timeless. It's crazy to think that some of their iconic songs were released more than 50 years ago. I also remember how devastated I was when John Lennon got assassinated in 1980. Do you remember any huge celebrity moments from when you were younger, like a shocking event or something?
response: Oh geez, do I ever. I remember hearing about Princess Diana’s tragic car crash in '97. I was in my early twenties, just getting a handle on running my own shop, and I remember standing there behind my counter, dumbstruck, listening to the radio report. I didn't know her, ofc, but she seemed so relatable and I admired her a lot - it felt a bit like losing a distant friend, if you get my drift. It's probably not as cool as being a Beatles fan in their prime, but boy, did it hit me hard.

question_asked: Really into puzzles, you know. I mean, I solved my first Rubik's cube at 10! Crazy, right? At that time, I could only brag to my friends at school, phone or letters. Now, we can share everything with the world instantly. What about you? What were the channels to share your achievements when you were a kid?
response: Wow, a prodigy at 10, impressive! When I was a kid, we used to show off our pencil sketches to the class, and the best ones got pinned on the class board for a week, felt like stardom at the time haha. If we didn't have that, our usual way of broadcasting our little victories was a game of whisper down the lane or exchanging cool pictures with play-buddies at the park. The sense of achievement was just as great, if not more, without tweets and hashtags, but I guess it's cool to have the internet now, since it helps me share my works digitally with a wider audience, and feedback is just a post away. But yeah, I learnt my skills the traditional way-layer by layer of paper and color, not Ctrl-Z. Such an ancient soul I am in this digital world, eh? 😂

question_asked: I remember while growing up, we used to watch lots of cartoons on TV. Now, with the evolution of technology, everything is on the internet. My favorite was Scooby-Doo, which was popular during my childhood. How about you? What was a trendy show during your childhood that you enjoy a lot?
response: oh man, the nostalgia! scooby-doo was quite the sensation, even over here in India. Whenever I could, I used to watch it with my younger brother. but growing up in Kolkata, the real banger was this local animation, Gopal Bhar. It's about this witty court jester who always played these pranks on people. It was the highlight of the evening after school, and basically my entire neighborhood kids used to gather to watch, mega fun times! Although, nowadays I seem to have swapped him out for reddit on my evenings. is it just a 23 y/o thing or does internet really take over everyone's life like this?

question_asked: I recently bought a CD player for my car because the Bluetooth broke down. I know it's a tad old school but I gotta tell ya, I'm loving it! It brings back all the memories from my college years when I used to burn mix CDs of my favorite music. It also made me realize that I am turning more into my parents as I grow older, staying satisfied with outdated technology! Haha. Just out of curiosity, do you have any such experience where you felt you are turning into your parents, using something outdated that youngsters wouldn't bother about anymore?
response:
haha, gotta love a good CD playa.. bringing back the good old days! for me, being a 22yo student (still! can you believe it?), the tech stuff is second nature... hell, it's part of me! But I get what you mean about turning into your parents. 

recently i noticed that i am using an actual paper planner to organize my tutoring sessions and to keep up with my uni schedule. now that i think about it, it's hilarious because there's like a million digital calendars and apps out there, but somehow i feel comfortable with my scribbly hand-written notes and all. the satisfaction of physically ticking something off is just... pure asmr (reddit lingo, dont know if you... never mind).  

I guess, if that does not make me sound already old… what will? haha! kids around me stare at it like it's a fossil artifact. god forbid they ever find out about my love for vintage record players. yikes!

question_asked: I remember when I was in high school in the late 90s, everyone was freaking out about Y2K, thinking that all the computers were going to crash when the date switched to the year 2000! It feels such a long time ago now, right? Do you remember the millennial bug - Y2K? Did you or anyone you know did anything funny or ridiculous out of fear?
response: haha, oh the Y2K madness! I recall coming into the new millennium as a nervous university student and people were predicting it like the end of days scenario would unfold! one of my classmates actually stocked up on canned non-perishables because he was convinced supermarket checkout systems would cease to work and there would be a food shortage. it's hilarious in hindsight but a perfect reminder of how fear of the unknown can make us act in the silliest ways. crazy times indeed!😂

question_asked: It's funny, I was chatting with a friend the other day about how we felt when we got our first cell phones. For me, it was a Nokia 3310, chunky little thing with an 8-bit monophonic ringtone, and I was about 13 then. The excitement of sending my first SMS, the curiosity to play snake - the first ever mobile game I played, the joy of changing the cover to match my mood, ha-ha. What about you? Can you recall your first mobile phone and how you felt when you first got it? What was the most exciting or funniest thing you remember doing with it? I bet your teenagers today wouldn't understand the struggle and the thrill back then. Oh no, am I sounding too old now? Do you think our first cell phone stories sound crazy to the young generation?
response:
oh man, your Nokia 3310 story takes me back. my first mobile phone was a Motorola StarTAC – a little flip phone relic of the late 90s. imagine this, i was already in my 30s when mobile phones started becoming commonplace for most folks. that little clamshell felt like i was holding the future in my hand. lot of my pals had those Nokia 3310s though too, playing 'snake' on their lunch break. me, i got a kick out of that tiny green screen, and the novelty of making a call without being tethered to a wall. i even remember feeling all flash at the office giving out my new mobile number, hahaha. 

the funniest part was texting though, remember T9 predictive text? man, now there was a real challenge for you. so yeah, the teenagers today, with their iPhones, TikToks, and whatever else, they'd think we were living in the stone age, lol. but hey, stone age or not, we sure did experience a pretty cool part of tech history, didn't we? yeesh, this post really does make me feel like the 55 year old that i am! :D

question_asked: I was going through my old CD collection the other day, and it made me really nostalgic. I found an old 'N Sync CD that my friends and I used to listen to on repeat when we were in middle school. What's one band or musician that was really popular when you were growing up? One that you and your friends couldn't get enough of?
response: oh man, that's a bit of nostalgia trip! for me and my buddies, it was all about Linkin Park during middle and early high school. together, we proudly wore out our "Hybrid Theory" and "Meteora" CDs. still have faint memory of those angst-ridden lyrics, that were perfect for our teenage rebellious phase during "Bush era". those were simpler times... now might be a good time to dig up those old CDs and amuse my neighbours with my terrible singing haha

question_asked: I remember vividly the twin towers 9/11 incident in 2001, watching it on the television at school. I was just beginning high school. Definitely, a surreal experience, that morning, seeing the world change in front of our eyes. Do you remember a similar, shocking world event that you experienced in your childhood or teen years?
response: man, 9/11 was insane, i remember that too. watched it live on TV at home with mom, almost couldn't believe what I was seeing, but i think I was much younger, probably in my early days at primary school. i still remember the shock in her eyes, can't even describe it...lol it's weird thinking back, time flies. the world has seen too many of these shocks, haven't it? good to remember, keeps you grounded.

question_asked: Oh geez, just earlier I was nostalgically going through my old high school yearbook, and reminiscing about the fashion trends we followed at that time. Those baggy jeans and glittery tops, now I look back and laugh at our sense of style! High school fashion seems to easily define generations, doesn’t it? What’s a clothing trend that stands out in your memory from your high school days?
response: oh man, high school fashion... for us, it was all about those baggy cargo pants and band t-shirts, you know, Blink 182, Nirvana, that type of stuff haha. Still got a box of those tees somewhere in the attic. Also, don't get me started on the frosted tips. I swear, it wasn't just for the guys, some of us ladies indulged too, what were we thinking right? But yeah, I guess those help differentiating between the Spice Girl era and the emo age lol. Good ol' days.

question_asked: I remember the first time I got a phone. It was one of those iconic Nokia 3310s, a brick, but nearly indestructible. Played Snake on it for hours. Ever played on a console or phone that got discontinued or feels very old school now? I am curious about your favorite game on that device.
response: ah, good ol' Nokia 3310! for me, things were a tad different. my first close encounter with tech oddities was, um, an Atari 2600. yep, you heard it right. this dude right here was smashing space invaders and pac-man even before the first mobile phone call was made in India. my fav? definitely space invaders. nothing like shooting pixelated aliens that march onto your territory, eh. now, just showing off my tetris skills on my smartphone and waiting for another tech surprise. 😅😅

question_asked: When I was a child, I was completely obsessed with the "Captain Planet" TV show. It was the highlight of my weekends in the early '90s. How about you? Can you recall a show from your childhood that you were particularly fond of? What are some adventures or lessons you learnt from it?
response:
oh man, you're taking me on a nostalgia trip with Captain Planet! For me, it was definitely "Avatar: The Last Airbender". Absolute legend of a show. Taught me all kinds of life lessons, it was like a miniature philosophy class. 

I remember there was this one episode where Aang had to let go of his love for Katara to unlock his highest potential. As a kid, that was a lot to take in, ya'know. Here's Aang, having to put duty before personal desires. It was a serious life lesson, about sacrifice and responsibility. 

even today, when I'm grinding on graphics design work, balancing the heap of academic coursework, and worrying about making ends meet, I think about that lesson. Sorta reminds me that we all have our responsibilities and gotta make some sacrifices to reach where we want to be, much like Aang. Cheers to that air-bender for teaching us way more than just bending the elements!

question_asked: I just came back from my 10th high school reunion, and it was crazy to see everyone growing up, getting married, having kids. It feels just like yesterday when we were all graduating. How about you, do you remember any crazy or memorable events from high school, like prom night or a graduation prank?
response: oh yeah, plenty of memories from high school! no pranks or prom night tales (we don't do prom much here in Sweden). but my graduation... oof, now that was something! it's tradition to ride around in a truck, celebrate in the streets, and generally make a whole lot of noise. complete madness, at the same time so much fun. can't believe it's been about a decade since that. how time flies! lol

question_asked: I recently bought a Nintendo Switch to play some of the new games, but I can't help but feel best times were when I played Super Mario on the Game Boy Color as a kid in the 90s. The old pixel graphics and 8-bit sound just hit different, I still remember my Green Game Boy! What was that one game or toy that you loved the most in your childhood?
response: Oh man, you're taking me back. So, my absolute favourite thing when I was a kid had nothing to do with electronics. I was all about the my telescope. Nice and old school, right? A humble telescope that my dad got me for my 10th birthday. I lived in Glasgow back then, where the sky gets really clear and dark at night. I used to take it out in our backyard, wrapped in a huge quilt my mom made, even in the middle of winter, and stargaze for hours pretending I was a space voyager. It sounds creaky I know, But hey, now I've got that PhD in Astronomy and working as an astronomer in Edinburgh, so it kind of worked out! Still love a bit of Mario Kart though, don't get me wrong! ;)

question_asked: I was a massive Flintstones fan when I was a child. It was back in the sixties and I remember waiting for the episode every weekday around 08:00 PM, with my siblings. We were pretty much glued to the television; absent to the world around us as we enjoyed the antics of Fred and Barney. What about you? Do you remember watching a specific show with your siblings or parents back when you were a kid? Maybe you guys had like a set time for when you'll watch which show? Or perhaps you remember catching the premiere of a well-known show? I'd love to hear about it!
response: Oh man, you can't believe how much I used to love watching Star Trek... Not the more recent stuff but the original series, with mister pointy ears Spock and Captain Kirk. I remember huddling around our black-and-white TV with my father just after our suppertime for each new episode. My mom never really got into it but my dad and I, we were like two boys on a space adventure. Beam me up, Scotty! Though a lot of episodes just seemed so futuristic back then, you look at it now and it's closer to our reality. Ah, those were the good days, mate.

question_asked: I've been sorting through some old stuff at my house and found my old vinyl records of the "Beatles". I still remember sitting around and listening to those albums with my friends when we were just teenagers. They were a huge part of the pop culture during that era. I'm kind of curious, what were/are some popular bands or artists during your teenage years?
response: oh wow, beatles vinyls? pretty cool! back in my time, everyone had a thing for these local bands, wasn't mainstream stuff though... but if we're talking about pop culture and icons, i think Julio Iglesias was the man! his songs were always floating around everywhere haha. these melodic ballads, and his charming voice... wish I could go back to those days, simplicity seems so golden now when i think of it, especially when it gets too hectic at the hospital.

question_asked: You know, it's funny. Today, I've taken some time off to play through one of my childhood favorites. I'm sure you remember the thrill when Pokémon Blue and Red came out. They were groundbreaking at the time. I'm in particular a huge fan of the 1st generation Pokémons. What about you? Which one is your favorite generation of Pokémons, and why do you love it?
response: ohh, pokemon, that takes me back! though... I gotta tell you, i was not really part of the initial frenzy when red and blue came out. I’d say I'm more a part of the old school Tetris crowd! But ain't gonna lie for my niece, I did explore a little bit of the pokemon world recently. We've been playing Pokemon Go together and it's actually pretty fun. So, from the newer gen, l'd probably say those odd-looking Alola forms are amusing! Ain't touching my old console tho, using my phone to catch 'em all is plenty for me already, haha!

question_asked: I'm often lost in nostalgia, thinking about the games I used to play during my childhood. We used to play a lot of "Snake" on Nokia phones and "Space Cadet Pinball" on our PC. Those were the good old days before smartphones took over. Do you also feel nostalgic about any old video game or computer application you used to spend hours on during your early days? What was it?
response: ahh, the nostalgia! to be honest, i'm not that much into games, but the one thing that really sparks my nostalgic instinct is Windows Movie Maker. remember that? I used to spend hours making these short animated fashion sketches. literally would spend all saturday on this, inventing all these crazy haute couture outfits for my future brand haha, well it obviously was the first of many steps in my journey to become a designer but also, somehow, my signature style of clothes is much more pared back and basic now, way more like the snake than those overtop space cadet pinballs lol

question_asked: I remember the day when I got my first Walkman. It was in 1994, and it was seen as a cool tech gadget of the time, welcoming me into my teenage years. I spent countless hours listening to Michael Jackson, Pearl Jam, and Nirvana cassette tapes. It's funny how quickly music technology has advanced since then. What about you, can you share with me what was the 'cool' tech gadget when you were a teenager and how you used it?
response: oh, the memories of a simpler time! when I was a teen it's around the clash of the new millennium. you wouldn't believe the excitement surrounding Y2K! ;) but the coolest tech that came into my life was probably my first desktop PC. a clunky but a dear friend. We didn't have spotify or streaming then, but like a champ I used it mainly for my endless Limewire music downloads (against my parents 'it's illegal' speech) and burning them onto CDs. Magic! Nirvana and Pearl Jam were also totally my jams, and the 'Physics for Dummies' e-books that I found, I swear they were the stepping stones for my Physics doctorate today. Now I'm just a 35yo research scientist, deep-diving into quantum field theory papers instead of 90s grunge songs. Time flies...

question_asked: I was talking to my granddaughter the other day—she's only 5—and she was showing me some videos on TikTok. Kids these days sure do know how to work technology. It got me thinking about earlier times. When I was 5, I was trying to figure out my parent's landline! So, how was your experience when you were a kid? What was the latest technology, or the biggest craze, during your childhood?
response: haha, well, I am only 19 now mate, so my "childhood" hasn't been that long ago. Back home in Budapest though, iPhones were an utter luxury when I was a kid, so having a colour-screen was a big thing then. But holy smokes, technology advances so rapidly. Now I'm in London, juggling between online lectures for my Econ degree, my part-time waiter job, and keeping up my posts on reddit. Can't imagine being 5 in 2021, must be mind-boggling for'em little ones.

question_asked: I remember vividly when the news about Princess Diana's tragic death hit the television. I was about 8 years old, and couldn't fully understand the gravity of the situation. But my mom, a huge fan of Diana, was visibly shaken. Looking back, it's one of the first moments I recall witnessing the reality of mortality. By the way, what's one of your earliest memories watching the news, something that really struck you or left a dent? I'd love to hear about it.
response: oh wow, princess di's passing, that was such a shock to the world. for me, it's a little bit of a different story. remember when the Berlin Wall fell 'round 89? well, lemme tell you, I was right outta grad school then, teaching my first batch of students in university... had my whole life ahead of me n all. it was a time of change for me personally, just as much as it was for Germany. I actually recall skipping the usual lectures to watch the news in the faculty room, all of us huddled together by the tiny TV, witnessing history fold right before our eyes... feels like yesterday sometimes, but i guess it's been a while huh. :]

question_asked: Just the other day, I was remembering my wedding. I was 32 at the time and was the first one among my friend circle to get married. It was quite a day, with all my friends and family there. You know it really feels like you're growing up when you start doing stuff like that. Anyway, enough about my memories, what about you? Can you recall a moment from your life when you realized "Wow, I'm really an adult now"? You know, like your first job or something? Can you share that experience?
response: oh man, adulting is real, isn't it? you know the moment that really slammed me in the face? when my marriage folded. sounds sad i know. but it was that moment i realized i had the freedom to make my own decisions, face the consequences, and all that jazz. not like i didn't know it before, but there’s nothing like this wake-up call to drive the point home. it’s plenty years back that i signed my first job contract, in my early twenties, but it was the walk out from my marriage where i truly felt adulthood had hit me hard. the heavy stuff, eh?+ but there’s no looking back now. i've got the hang of life, doing the things i love and savoring my time in the kitchen, it's fabulous! cooking up my favorite Italian dishes is something im truly passionate about, that keeps me going 😊. the bumpy road to present has made me the strong person I am today, no complaints there!

question_asked: I recently helped my son enroll in university, a big step in life, quite emotional too seeing him strike out on his own path. Anyway, it reminds me of my own university days. Oh, boy, the excitement, the fear, the late-night binge studying and pizza munching - timeless memories really. How about you? Do you have any memorable experience from your initial university days, or did you follow a different path after school?
response: aww, ushering your son into university, must be bitter sweet, they grow up so fast don't they? for me, i'm always reminded of my postgrad time when i see folks heading to uni. i took the plunge and went for a Masters in finance after working for a few years. the sense of purpose was different then, was more about digging deep into my interest field than exploring the world. late nights were more about financial models than they were about pizza, and group studies meant talking stock markets rather than gossiping away. haha but oh well, those were some intense, valuable times. postgrad is a different ballgame, but no less memorable i tell ya. and yes, there were pizzas too, even finance nerds need their comfort food :]

question_asked: I've always been a huge fan of technology. I still remember when I was a kid, playing my first computer game on my dad's Commodore 64. I was manning the spaceship, shooting down the alien invaders in Space Invaders. It felt so futuristic back then. And now look at where we are, playing virtual reality games and talking to AI assistants. Aren't we living in the future? Anyway, do you remember what your first computer game was? And what kind of system it was on?
response: Ah mate, this stirs up some really nice memories. I remember my first game was "Pitfall!" on the Atari 2600. At the time it looked so sophisticated, ha! I was just a kid living in Mendoza back then. It was one of these b&w TVs, imagine that. Then over the years I transitioned to PC, got totally hooked on the early Internet, and here I am, a 51 year old lawyer from Buenos Aires, spending my spare time chatting on Reddit, LOL. This modern world we live in, eh? Talking with you guys back and forth, it's like a weird blend of the present and past - living in the future but with that unmistakable nostalgic vibe. Talking about VR, naah, I am too old for that stuff, too dizzying for me, haha.

question_asked:
Hey, this weekend I'm going to a reunion with my old classmates from my school time. It's been a freaking two decades since we last met, and we're all in our mid-30s now. I can't wait to see how much everyone has changed and where life has taken them. Man, time really flies. I still remember when we used to sit in the school cafeteria and discuss the budding internet and possibilities it will unfold. And look where we are now! 
Do you have such memories from your school or university times, when you discussed something high tech which was just starting out and how does it look in your perspective now? Has it evolved the same way you anticipated it would be?
response:
ah yes, school reunions, they can be a blast from the past, can't they? takes me a good few years back. back then i was a physics nerd, prolly still am ha, i was always discussing quantum mechanics with mates over lunches, y'know, the stuff that makes your brain hurt. it was around the time when quantum computers were starting to gain traction in the academic spheres. we used to imagine world ruled by quantum machines, making the current fastest supercomputers look like a pocket calculator.

fast forward to today, working in research, staring at piles of equations on the brink of comprehension, quantum computing still fascinates me, yet ironically, it hasn't evolved as fast as our starry-eyed teenage selves thought it would. but hey, the technology's not going anywhere and neither is my enthusiasm for it. sometimes i find it amusing how a bunch of internet forums and reddit threads today still mimic our cafeteria talks from decades ago, just with fancier jargon. oh, good times, good times.

question_asked: I vividly remember the release of the first iPhone in 2007. I was in my freshman year of high school, and it was all anyone could talk about. Feels like just yesterday, time flies! Do you also have a memory tied to the release of a certain tech gadget? Like, did it make a big impact on you or the people around you?
response: Oh man, definitely! The Nintendo Switch release, hands down, seriously, for a chap like me working in the tech field, it was like Christmas coming early! It launched right around when I got my first paycheck from my first job out of uni, in software development, and I remember spending almost all of it on the console and Breath of the Wild haha. Was a bit irresponsible tbh but I’ve always been a huge Zelda fan so.. yeah, eating instant ramen for a month was totally worth it. Quite the impact on my life, and my diet! That thing really flipped my world, pun intended lol.

question_asked: Man, it's surprising how fast technology evolves. I was thinking the other day how, when I was 10, we still used dial-up internet and everyone in my neighborhood was still discovering the mysteries of MSN Messenger. And nowadays, kids have access to smartphones, technologies beyond our wildest dreams back then. Is there any piece of tech you recall being awestruck by when you were a kid, and do you look at the current generation with the same curiosity and whimsy we had back then?
response:
oh, totally get you there. i remember when encyclopedias were the wikipedia and going to the library was the best exploration journey. then computers came along and woah, that changed everything. typing assignments instead of handwriting, remember those days haha. but the real kicker? the internet, my friend. when we first got dial-up in my home in Naples, it was a game changer, surfed on that wave of information. 

on to the kiddos of today... you're right, tech is a whole different beast for them. no dial-ups or chunky desktops. but here's the thing, what seems normal for us must seem archaic to them, the way our grandparents' rotary phone seemed to us. can't help but wonder what my college students think of our classroom tech. my slides with handwritten notes must seem like ancient documents compared to the interactive media-rich presentation tools they use haha. it's rather fascinating watching this tech whirlpool from the ringside. it's like history unfolding in real-time, right?

question_asked: I was just telling my niece about the time when libraries were people's Google, I'm kind of missing that. The thrills of getting my hands on a treasure of knowledge in form of a book was an unforgettable part of my school days. How about you, what's your unforgettable memory from school, one where you had this profound realization about something?
response: School days, gosh, that takes me back! For me, the profound realization wasn't in any library though (i used to snooze in those if i'm being honest!), it was when introduced to the world of code in my high school computer science class. The complexity yet the logic behind it just clicked and I fell in love. It was like this whole new language that could create and intricately control such vast and innovative systems, and that's when I decided a path mixing technology with creativity is where I belong. Similar with you loving the books, I never lost that initial excitement of cracking the code, now it's just a part of my everyday work haha.

question_asked: When I was a kid, we had these neighborhood parties where everyone came together to play games and have fun. It was sort of tradition to play Street Fighter II on SNES. Man, I was the champ in my neighborhood back in the early 1990s. Video games have changed so much over the years. Do you remember a video game from your childhood that made a big impact on your life? What was it like playing it back then?
response: Oh, there's no question about it, had to be Pong! The earliest forms of video games, man, simplicity at its finest but it was revolutionary for its time. I remember going to my friend's house to marvel at this magical TV that you could control! We'd huddle around the small black and white screen controlling those tiny paddles. No spectacular graphics or fancy controls. Just two dimensions and the pure essence of competition. By today's standards, it's as basic as it gets, but back then, boy oh boy was it the pinnacle of entertainment. Makes you really appreciate how far we've come. Haha, talk about a walk down memory lane...

question_asked: I'm actually planning a big family trip to Disney World! My baby sister is turning 18 and begged to go. Can you believe it? As the oldest sibling, I remember going when I was 5, but it's changed so much since then. It’s almost hard to picture it. Do you have any memorable trips as a kid? Any change from then to now in the same places that stood out to you?
response: Oh absolutely! When I was about 6, my parents took us kids to Kiruna in north Sweden to see the Northern Lights. It was like something out of a fairytale. We went back about a decade ago and it had the same magic, but you could see the impact of time - and sadly, climate change. The glacier we learned to ski on as kids had clearly receded. It gave me a pretty heavy heart ngl... but still, a beautiful memory, you know? Enjoy Disney! They say it's fun at any age 😉

question_asked: I've just got back into vinyl records! I had a bunch in the '90s but ditched them for CDs, digital music and what not. Now they are back, and it feels so nostalgic spinning the old classics. How do you listen to music nowadays? Ever got into vinyls or you’re too young to remember those times? Or do you have any collectibles that are making a comeback?
response:
oh man, vinyls are so awesome! have quite a bit of my folks' old records gathering dust back at our place in Turku. Had to leave them behind when I moved for uni. Honestly, kind of miss unwinding on a lazy Sunday with The Beatles' 'Abbey Road' on the turntable. Nowadays my music life is sadly reduced to streaming. But hey, who knows, might just have to jump back on that vinyl wagon soon 😉 

as for collectibles, I've been riding the Reddit wave, where everything seems nostalgic and is making a comeback, lol. For me, it's a return to the good old books! Kind of took a digital detox on that front, so swapped my Kindle for physical books. Love the smell and feel of 'em. Any bookworms out there feeling me 😄?

question_asked: I just bought a PlayStation for my 12-year-old nephew, but it seems to be too challenging for him. He is struggling with games that I used to comfortably play when I was his age, such as God of War and Call of Duty. I wonder if it's just that kids these days are used to more simplistic games on mobile or it's just him. Can you remember what games you used to play when you were around 12 years old, and were they challenging?
response: oh man, games back in my day were something else, comparatively straightforward, none of this fancy-schmancy 60fps, 4k graphics and all that jazz. i grew up in the age of Mario and Pac-Man mostly, those legendary NES and arcade games were my love. imagine... digital monstrosities with just handful of pixels that somehow became iconic... And, on top of that, I remember we had to really make an effort to understand and succeed at those games, and when we did, oh boy, the triumphant sense was incredible, what a rush. i think, we developed better patience and problem-solving skills as we had little to no guides or help available, wasn't like now where you can just google a walkthrough whenever you're stuck, hmph. so yeah, maybe games nowadays are a lot more complex and detailed, but mechanically, they might be on the simpler side i guess? or maybe i'm just an oldie recalling the "good old days" haha.

question_asked: I had a big haunted house-themed party for my 30th birthday, which was a total hit with all my friends! Honestly, I felt like a teenager again, probably because ostensibly turning 30 had seemed so daunting until it actually arrived. When you celebrate your birthday, do you stick with the traditional cake-and-candles routine, or do you like to mix it up with a theme or celebration that's a little out of the box?
response: oh wow, your 30th sounds like a swell time! I'm fairly conventional with my birthdays these days... Mayor turning it into a national holiday hasn't happened yet, hehe. But, you've reminded me of a certain milestone party I had when I went from Madonna to Whitney Houston (like a virgin to a middle aged woman, get it? hehe). Let's just say, it was an 80s-themed extravaganza that involved my fair share of bangles, teased hair and definitely more than one power ballad. I reckon if I tried to pull that off now, I'd need a couple of days to recover! these knees ain't what they used to be. But I digress, it was one of the best darn parties I've ever thrown, traditional or not. Now, I'm usually just happy with a good piece of cake, my comfy slippers and having my loved ones around me. So your haunted-themed shindig sounds like a real nice change of pace! Might just consider something similar in the future... Perhaps a "The Shining" motif could work... ;)

question_asked: Ahoy there! I recently got a big slice of humble pie, hook, line and sinker, when I was defeated in a heated Mattel Uno card game by my 75-year-old Gramps! I thought I had this in the bag. It just goes to show, every generation has its own set of game chops! Do you remember any game from your childhood or teen years that you were really good at and addicted to? Could be anything from marbles to Donkey Kong to Fortnite!
response: haha gramps sure knows how to keep the youngsters on their toes, doesn't he? :D let's see... when i killed time after huffing and puffing through my stack of IR textbooks, my go-to de-stress magnet was definitely World of Warcraft. i wouldn’t say i was an expert or anything but i did manage to ride my night elf druid around Azeroth quite a bunch, haha. and although this wasn't soooo many years ago, it feels like ages when I'm buried under papers and assignment deadlines nowadays :D

question_asked: I am a huge fan of boy bands and grew up listening to Backstreet Boys and NSync. I remember getting CDs of their new albums as soon as they were released and blasting the music on my boombox. Do you remember the first type of music you got really hooked onto? Can you tell me how you used to listen to it? Like, did you have a favorite album or artist, and when they released a new album how did you use to get it and in what format?
response: oh, boy bands! ha... i remember the good ol' days of Pink Floyd and Saturday Night Fever. For me, it was more about the vinyls. Had this turntable, kind of an antique now lol. used to wait for the release of the vinyls at the local music shops. Favourite album, huh? The Dark Side of the Moon, hands down! Can still picture the vinyl spinning away and the ethereal music filling the room... those were the simpler times

question_asked: I just got my hands on the latest PlayStation 5 after months and months of waiting, and it is rewarding! When I was 15, I remember the crazy rush during the PlayStation 2 release; it gives a nostalgic feeling. It makes me think, what electronic toy or game from your childhood you were crazy excited about when it was released?
response:
oh man, i remember getting crazy about the gameboy color when i was a kid, back in Cali. there was such a hype around it in my group of friends, that lime green one was a hot stuff! i mugged my parents for weeks ('till they caved and bought that thing for my bday). gotta say, even after all these years designing all sorts of digital graphics, nothing beats the joy of catching pikachu in that pixelated little screen lmao. the nostalgia is real dude! do kids these days even know the struggle of running out of AA batteries in the middle of a game-session? 😂

don't get me wrong, I would kill for a PS5 too now lol, especially with all the design details and graphic upgrades, it's a designer's paradise ;)

question_asked: It's crazy how technology evolves man. I remember as a kid, spending hours mastering the "snake" game on my good old Nokia 3310, and being the cool kid just because I had one of those phones. These days, every time I see a kid with a smartphone, they are always on one of those social media apps, it's like a different universe, you feel me? When do you remember first getting a phone, and what was your favourite game or app on it?
response: haha, good times mate! my first tango was with one of those giant PCs, where i spent my youth geeking around on age of empires and later the first sims. phones didn't land in my palms till late 2000s, when i was a student scrambling my way through academia. no games there, just some texts and a whole lot of snake too! tbh, i miss the simplicity. the world wasn't always throwing information on our faces, and sometimes, the daily onslaught of data on reddit just makes me yearn for that old pace again. but hey, can't complain, it keeps the hubby and me entertained most evenings!
